### Strong 1 · the wire value `-1` and the stored value `"u"`

Ground: `annotator/unified_server.py:2252` held
`stored = None if label in (None, "clear", -2) else ("u" if label == -1 else label)` and
`annotator/app.js:1362` held
`... else state.balls.labels[file] = label === -1 ? 'u' : label;`, so one mapping lived in two realms; the
server half was guarded (`tests/test_unified_server.py:136-137`) and the console half was never driven — the
only console call with a label was `tests/test_app_timeline.js:717 realm.run('window.CornerPocketReview.labelBall(null, 2);')`,
which passes 2, and `git grep -c "balls.labels" -- tests` printed nothing. Repair: each realm owns its names —
`annotator/unified_server.py:98-100 BALL_LABEL_UNKNOWN_WIRE = -1`, `BALL_LABEL_UNKNOWN_STORED = 'u'` and
`BALL_LABEL_CLEARED_WIRE = (None, 'clear', -2)`, and `annotator/app.js:1362-1364` the console's pair — and
every reader reads a name (`annotator/unified_server.py:2262-2263` the gate and `:2269` the storage mapping;
`annotator/app.js:1367 ballLabelWire`, `:1368 ballLabelStored`, `:1382` the echo and `:1383` the receipt). The
service publishes no table on purpose: the console is one static file that paints its panel before any
request returns, so a published table would cost a route and a fetch and would answer after the click. The new
`tests/test_console_service_agreement.py` (6 cases) drives both realms and holds the mapping table: `-1` and
`'u'` reach the store as `'u'` and read `Unknown`; `-2` and `'clear'` delete the row and read `cleared`; `0`
and `15` store themselves and read `Cue 0` and `Ball 15`; `1` to `14` store themselves; and `16` is refused by
the route with `APIError("invalid ball label")` while the row keeps its old label.

### Strong 2 and Worth 1 · two guard cases of the timeline suite

Ground: `tests/test_app_timeline.js:907` held
`assert.strictEqual(T.tagRow(5, 6, 'model', ''), T.tagRow(5, 6, 'model', ''), 'outside a paint a row is drawn where asked (no queue)');`
while the real check stood at `:908`, and a balanced-paren scan of `tests/*.js` for byte-equal pairs answered
exactly that line — a guard that cannot fail. Repair: the case draws a row while no paint stands and checks
two real facts (the row holds no queue token, and it holds `x="5" y="6"`), and the writer's own scan
`/tmp/dshsess/scan_selfcompare.js` answers `hits: 1` on the head copy and `hits: 0` after the repair.
`Worth 1`: `tests/test_app_timeline.js:1540` matched
`/^The model table quad is \d+ px off this dataset's saved corners …$/` while `:1536` and `:1537` set both
quads in the same case; the case now owns the two quads, recomputes the offset, and compares the whole
sentence, so a wrong offset fails. Its limit stands recorded: the case holds its own copy of the distance
rule, because `annotator/app.js:2387` exports no `quadDistance` at the seam, and the pair it uses gives a mean
of 98.097, so it pins the number 98 and not the rounding mode.

### Worth 2 · the 0.2 s clip floor

Ground: `annotator/app.js:745` held `to: Math.max(from + 0.2, to)` and
`annotator/unified_server.py:1895` held `if duration < 0.2:`, and no test named either. Repair:

`annotator/app.js:735` (read at `:744`, published to the realm at `:2402`), with the agreement case holding
the two names equal. The measured floor: `0.2` encodes and `0.19` answers

`CLIP_MIN_S = 0.25` / `CLIP_MAX_S = 5.0` at `annotator/unified_server.py:427-428` is a different rule and did
not move.

### The measurement that closed the round-72 question

The walk answered the brief's request exactly: `tests/test_projection_guard.py` read two texts only — an
`ast.Compare` shaped `abs(...) < 1e-9` or `< 1e-12`, and a `project_point(...)` call whose `tolerance=`
keyword NAME was compared with the `SITES` literal — and it read no `round(...)` node. So the rounding bite
(`round(point[0], 1)` to `round(point[0], 0)`) answered no fault, while the tolerance bite did answer one
(`Probe._to_px of Probe.px passes DEFAULT_TOLERANCE, but the site declared PIXEL_TOLERANCE`). The record of
round 72 had claimed that both bites stayed green; the Lead corrected that paragraph in `b6925f4`, because the
first reading of the tolerance run mistook the guard's own failure output for a pass. The walk also found that
the first assertion of the case at `tests/test_projection_guard.py:288` was vacuous under a plant that changed
no text, because `real.replace(...)` returned the real text.

### Strong 1 · the byte count an operator reads

Ground: the byte count had four display sites (`annotator/refusals.py:346 gb`,
`annotator/vod_import.py size_text`, `annotator/ops.js:132 sizeText`, `annotator/vision-stage.js:955 sizeText`)
and four readers, and two of them disagreed: the MB branch answered `12.3 MB` in python against `12 MB` in the
console, and the GB branch answered `1.2 GB` against `1.3 GB` on the exact tie of 1_250_000_000 bytes, because
python's `:.1f` rounds half to even while javascript's `toFixed` rounds half up. The operator acts on the
console's estimate line (`annotator/ops.js:664`), so python followed the console. Repair:
`annotator/refusals.py` owns both branches (`rounded` at `:333`, `gb` at `:346`, `size_text` at `:351`, ties
rounding up through `Decimal` and `ROUND_HALF_UP`), `annotator/app.js:26` owns the console rule as
`window.ConsoleRules.sizeText`, `annotator/vod_import.py` imports it, and `annotator/ops.js:132` and
`annotator/vision-stage.js:955` read the console home lazily. The measured boundary table holds 18 counts and
both realms answer one text for every one of them (`0 MB` for 0, `1 MB` at 1_000_000, `2 MB` at 1_500_000,
`12 MB` at 12_345_678, `1000 MB` at 999_999_999, `1.0 GB` at 1_000_000_000, `1.3 GB` at 1_250_000_000,
`8.6 GB` at 8_606_363_471, `52.2 GB` at 52_196_323_328). `tests/test_console_round73_owners.py` holds 12
cases: one home per realm, every other site reading a home, a planted copy reported, a lost rule reported, and
the two boundary tables. The writer found and repaired one regression of its own making while it scanned:
`tests/test_console_audit_labels` broke with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading
'liveDetectors')`, because that driver loads `annotator/ops.js` alone, and the fix defers the read into
`liveTicks()`, which is the pattern that file already uses at `:11` and `:13`.

### Strong 1 · one frame at one time stood six times and answered two ways

Ground: `src/pipeline.py:57 extract_frame` was an existing owner with one caller and no test, while six sites in
five files spelled its four-statement seek window by hand and disagreed on the failure answer — four refused
with three spellings and two answered `None` — and only `src/sam3_ball_cache.py:241` read the container time
back. Repair: `src/pipeline.py:306 read_frame(video_path, t_sec)` is the one window and answers
`(frame, decoded_t, frame_number)` with the container's own frame number, `:326 frame_gap_refusal(t_sec)` holds
the one refusal text `could not read frame at t={t_sec}`, and `:331 extract_frame_or_none` answers the frame or
`None`; the six sites read an owner name through a local import and hold no capture of their own
(`src/ball_fp_audit.py measure_frame` and `native_frame`, `src/tiny_ball_net.py load_frame`,
`src/sam3_ball_cache.py detect_frame` and `diagnose_frame`, `src/fast_ball_labels.py frame_at`). The three old
refusal spellings are gone. The repair also fixed a real defect: `load_frame` read `CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES` after
`cap.release()` and answered `-1`; it answers the container's number now (2101 at t=70.0 of the vod30 clip).
The new readers stand at `:303` and below, so the lines `src/ball_gate.py` cites in `src/pipeline.py` did not
move and `tests/test_citation_lines.py` stays green. `tests/test_frame_reader_owner.py` holds nine cases and
reports a site that opens its own capture. The measured census after the repair: nine sites read an owner name
and two open a capture of their own (the owner and the sequential sweep of `src/tiny_ball_net.py read_frames`).
The frame numbers of the fixture: a 40-frame MJPG clip at 30.0 fps answers frame 16 at t=0.5 and frame 1 at
t=0.0.

### Worth 1 · the cloth-contour preamble stood twice

Ground: `src/quad_fit.py:57-64` and `src/quad_fit_lines.py:164-171` were identical for eight statements and

`src/quad_fit.py:56 cloth_contours(bgr)` answers `(mask, big, h, w)` or `None` and both fitters read it,

### Note 1 and Note 2 · the two holds that were weaker than their names

The walk answered the Lead's two requests exactly. `tests/test_playfield_quads.py:622` and its docstring
claimed the tool answers the owner's `unavailable_verdict`, but the case only ran the line rule at `:217`, and
the dictionary was in fact held by `tests/test_playfield_parallel_owner.py:425`. Repair (both halves): the case
is renamed `test_the_exempt_tool_holds_no_check_call_inside_its_handler` and states the line rule only, and a
new case `test_the_exempt_tool_answers_the_owner_dictionary_for_a_fault` plants the fault on call 2, holds the
call count at two and compares the tool's answer with `unavailable_verdict(ValueError('planted fault'))`. And
`tests/test_pid_identity.py:127` asserted only `0.0 < PERSON_CONF < 1.0`, so all five cases of the class passed
with `PERSON_CONF` patched to `0.30`. Repair: the module gained `MEASURED_PERSON_CONF = 0.35` and the case
`test_the_owner_holds_the_value_the_four_sites_use`, whose sentence names both numbers and the reason (the NMS
bar is strict: a box on the value is dropped and a box above it survives).

### Lessons

1. A new import at the top of a file moves every citation below it by the number of added lines.
   Count the added lines, and do not read the shift from the first changed line.
2. A citation whose target line has no text points nowhere.  Test the target line, and compare the
   text at the old line of HEAD with the text at the new line.
3. A guard that walks the shipped tree must skip a path that disappeared between the walk and the
   read.  Another writer can hold a temporary module inside `src/`.
4. A record sentence can be false when it is written.  The walk of this round found one.
5. A writer can miss the measurement of the content sha1 before its edit.  The Lead recovers it
   with `git show HEAD:<file> | sha1sum`.

   held an `IndentationError` from writer WE.  A bite is valid only on a quiet tree.

   listed the doc lines that quote the code its sites replaced.

### Lessons

1. A walk must not run while a writer holds the tree.  This round ran the second walk
   beside three writers; the walk saw ` M docs/vision-audit.md` and
   ` M tests/test_pool_test_suites.py` appear under it and reported the fact itself.  The
   rule stands: no writer is active while a walk runs.
2. Measure the sha1 before and after every bite.  The first bite of
   `annotator/twitch_vod_source.py` used a `sed` whose pattern matched no line, so the sha1
   answered the same value before and during and the bite proved nothing.  The second
   attempt found the line with `grep -n` and turned three cases red.
3. A `sed` on a value that already holds the same bytes changes nothing.  Writer X9 and the
   Lead both met this shape this round.
4. A walk that writes to one report path replaces the earlier report.  The first walk of
   this round wrote `/tmp/dshsess/walk_round97.md` and the second replaced it.  A round with
   two walks must give each its own path.

Walk `863a51f4` wrote `/tmp/dshsess/walk_round99.md` (345 lines; 37 files, 14 of them in full) at HEAD

line answers `Strong candidate present - 3 Strong, 1 Worth, 1 Note`.  The Lead read back every ground of
the three Strong rows and of the Worth row.

### Row 1 (Strong) - the live refusal sentences stand twice

`annotator/live_processing.py` raises the sentences a live start can refuse with (18 raise statements).
The console phrases them in Chinese, and `annotator/app.js` holds the anchored pattern list
`const liveRefusals = [` for a sentence that carries no code.  Drift is not a risk but a fact: the
sentence `Live detectors must be a non-empty list of table, person, ball, balls` is written by
`annotator/live_processing.py:375` and no pattern claimed it, so the Chinese console stayed English.
The nearest case `tests/test_app_timeline.js:3541-3559` carried its own ten sentences and compared the
count only, so it never read the service file.

Writer WA (three files) closed the row.  `annotator/app.js` gained one row at `:2134` with an explicit
alternation (`(?:table|person|ball|balls)`) so a wrapped or unrelated sentence stays English; the
console suite gained the eleventh sentence at `tests/test_app_timeline.js:3550`, and its positional
`refusals[7]` and `refusals[8]` reads became `refusals.indexOf(...)` at `:3562-3563`, because an
inserted sentence makes a position name the wrong string.  The new guard `tests/test_live_refusal_owner.py`
parses every raise of the owner, rebuilds the sentence each one sends, and asks the shipped patterns
which sentences they claim - in node, with the real javascript regex semantics, not a python rewrite of
them.  Nine cases hold the raise list, one pattern per judged sentence, the two judged `UNMAPPED`
sentences with a verifiable reason each, the console table for the coded sentences, the retired row, the

named `annotator/live_processing.py:375`.  The Lead changed the sentence of that raise to
`Live detectors must hold at least one detector from %s`: the owner answered
`86c0087b520662907d4ff300ab12e489a1a15ab8 -> cdf8ec0e31a76b3220fad0542034992c4d7bb50d ->

sentences answer the code table`, `112f6cf test: the live refusal sentences answer one pattern list`,
`2fbf71c docs: the citations follow the shift of round 99`.

### Lessons of round 99

1.  A guard reads the shipped artefact with the real semantics of its own language.  The new refusal
    guard runs `annotator/app.js` in node, so a javascript regex cannot drift from the guard's idea of it.
2.  An inserted sentence makes a positional read name the wrong string.  `refusals[7]` became
    `refusals.indexOf(...)` in the same edit.
3.  A writer's first revision can break another owner.  The literal `JPEG encoding failed` belongs to
    `tests/console_text.py`, and the case of that owner answered red until the writer read the owner.
4.  A walk samples and a writer measures.  The walk named four sentences with no code and the writer
    measured six.
5.  A bite on a value that does not exist changes no byte.  Take the sha1 before and after every bite.
